newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RALLYING-WORLD CHAMPION MAKINEN EYES REPEAT TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-WORLD CHAMPION MAKINEN EYES REPEAT TRIUMPH.

text.p: World champion Tommi Makinen, whose Argentina rally victory proved the turning point of his 1996 season, has his sights on a repeat triumph.
Spurred on by that win, the Mitsubishi driver from Finland dominated the remainder of the season to earn the drivers' title.
"After last year's result, I am looking forward to the event very much. I think it will be very good for our car," he said ahead of Thursday's start of the seventh round of the championship.
It marks the halfway stage of the season, with a course through the high-altitude mountain regions of the Andes.

Makinen, who was forced to withdraw from the previous round in Corsica after a bizarre accident when he hit a cow, leads the standings by two points from Briton Colin McRae. Spain's Carlos Sainz is joint third with part-time Italian driver Piero Liatti.
For McRae, the Argentina event is a return to the scene of his most disappointing outing last season, where he was fined after colliding with spectators in a service area.
But after a stirring drive to victory in Corsica two weeks ago, the Subaru driver is keen to take the win that would hand him the lead of the world championship.
"Although Argentina has never really been kind to me, it's a great, high-speed event with long, fast straights that end in slow, tricky corners," he explained.
"Although the stages aren't really rough, you have to be careful because if you get off the line, there are many huge rocks that could put you out the event."
Sainz won the Argentina event in 1991 and has taken four runner-up finishes since, but his Ford has not showed well on the similar gravel rallies this season.
"I haven't had much experience this season on pure gravel, just a few stages in Portugal, but I'm sure we'll learn a lot very quickly and be completely competitive."
The three main championship contenders all have new team mates for this event as the fight between the three manufacturers hots up.

Makinen welcomes back Briton Richard Burns at Mitsubishi, McRae will work alongside Swede Kenneth Eriksson at Subaru once again, while Ford have recruited Finn Juha Kankunnen in a bid to land the title for Sainz.
The rally, which reaches up to 2,000 metres above sea level in the foothills of the Andes, takes place over 23 special stages on three legs based around the town of Cordoba.
